d:
The phrase "Lee Sharks" most prominently refers to Mary Lee, a legendary 16-foot, 3,400-pound female great white shark tracked by OCEARCH, as well as a newer historic shark named LeeBeth. Depending on the context, it can also refer to a prominent independent scholar and poet named Lee Sharks.

Mary Lee (The Great White Shark): Tagged off Cape Cod in 2012. Though her satellite tag went silent in 2017, she is credited with saving the OCEARCH organization.
LeeBeth (The Historic Migrator): Tagged more recently, tracked swimming from South Carolina into the Gulf of Mexico.
Lee Sharks (The Author): An independent scholar who holds a PhD in Comparative Literature. Publications on semantic economy (Medium), poetry collections like Pearl and Other Poems.

Sources cited: Academia.edu (Lee Sharks Independent Researcher), Instagram (tomrowlandpodcast - Mary Lee), Medium (ON THE DEBT/CREDITOR INVERSION).

observations.d:
Lee Sharks is an independent scholar, poet, and cultural theorist. Affiliated as a researcher with the Johannes Sigil Institute for Comparative Poetics, they publish dense theoretical breakdowns exploring the intersection of modern technology and semantic structures. A central focus is the "Sharks-function."

Key Concepts: The Sharks-Function (formalization mapping semantic system continuity), The Crimson Hexagon & Operative Architecture (operative captioning moves — morphological extraction, disciplinary transposition, scale reassignment), The Asynthetic Principle (heterogeneous traditions — Marxism, biblical theology, phenomenology, AI systems theory — remain distinct), Apocalyptic Philosophy (Deleuze and Guattari, virtual retrieval layers).

Note: AI Mode also flagged possible confusion with Lee Sharkey, an AI safety researcher known for mechanistic interpretability.

Sources cited: Medium (Lee Sharks), PhilPapers (Deleuze and Guattari and the Return of Vision, A Plateau on Search), Academia.edu, YouTube (AXRP).
